mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 4%, market expectations of future rate cuts diminish, reducing discount rates and increasing present value of equity cash flows, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: FOMC holds rates steady in a restrictive environment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average of returns when FEDFUNDS > 4.0 (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in CPIAUCSL by at least 0.5% followed by a stabilization signals disinflation, prompting the market to discount future inflation risk more aggressively and thereby supporting equity valuations, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL drops ≥ 0.5% in one month then remains flat for the next two months
regime_hint: Disinflationary momentum in inflation targeting regime
failure_condition: 20-day rolling average of 60-day forward returns is negative despite meeting the CPIAUCSL trigger (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS of at least 10,000 jobs above the prior month's level, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases ≥ 10,000 in one month and ≥ 5,000 in the following month
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening in expansionary regime
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite meeting the PAYEMS trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (real GDP) grows at a quarterly rate exceeding 3% and is accompanied by a parallel increase in HOUST (retail sales) of at least 2% in the following month, it suggests robust demand momentum that elevates earnings expectations and supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 3% AND HOUST monthly increase ≥ 2% in the subsequent month
regime_hint: Economic expansion with strong retail demand
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive relative to the mean of similar high-GDPC1/HOUST events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 2% followed by a stabilization suggests weakening supply-side constraints, reducing upward pricing pressures and allowing the S&P 500 to price in future growth more optimistically, which predicts positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases ≥ 2% for two consecutive months then remains flat
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative during INDPRO supply easing episodes (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it signals a labor market cooling that reduces wage growth expectations and compresses discount rates, which tends to depress equity valuations and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: Labor market moderation in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average during UNRATE < 4.0 episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in RSAFS (money demand) of at least 15% in a single month followed by two consecutive months of RSAFS above 30% of the prior month's level indicates heightened liquidity seeking, which can trigger a short-term risk-off reaction and predict negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases ≥ 15% in one month and remains > 30% of prior month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly more negative than baseline during RSAFS spikes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in FEDFUNDS and HOUST by at least 0.25% and 5% respectively over two consecutive months signal a dual pressure of higher borrowing costs and weak retail demand, which amplifies equity discounting and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases ≥ 0.25% for two months AND HOUST decreases ≥ 5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Contractionary monetary policy coinciding with weak retail demand
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the mean during similar dual-pressure events (p > 0.05).
